alt: A timeline from 1550 to 1750 shows six example wars: the Dutch Revolt (1568-1648), the Imjin War (1592-1598), the Thirty Years' War (1618-1648), the English Civil Wars (1642-1651), the Great Northern War (1700-1721) and the War of the Spanish Succession (1701-1714). A note warns that the Seven Years' War is outside the period.
caption: Six example wars, all inside 1500-1750.

alt: Long-term causes of the Thirty Years' War (the Peace of Augsburg excluding Calvinism, rival alliances of 1608 and 1609, Habsburg ambitions) lead to the short-term trigger: the Defenestration of Prague (May 1618) and the election of Frederick V (1619). Spain, Denmark, Sweden and France then intervene. France, though Catholic, fought the Habsburgs.
caption: A Bohemian revolt became a European war as foreign powers joined.

alt: Cause: Hideyoshi unified Japan in 1590, demanded passage through Korea to attack Ming China and, when Korea refused, landed at Busan in 1592; historians debate his motives. Outcome: Yi Sun-sin's fleet cut supply lines, Ming armies intervened from 1593 and Korean righteous armies harassed the invaders, leading to Japanese withdrawal after Hideyoshi's death in 1598.
caption: Supply, naval power and Ming intervention decided the Imjin War.

alt: Four practices: the trace italienne made sieges long and expensive; Maurice of Nassau's drill and Gustavus Adolphus's combined arms won battles such as Breitenfeld (1631); armies needed money, from Wallenstein's levies to Britain's Bank of England and national debt; and coalition leadership won Blenheim (1704).
caption: Walls, drill, money and leadership shaped the outcome of wars.

after: ## A civil war example: the English Civil Wars
alt: Three linked columns for the English Civil Wars. Causes: religion, Charles I's taxes without Parliament and conflict over the army. Practices: the New Model Army of 1645, professional and promoting by merit, won at Naseby. Effects: Charles I executed in 1649, a republic under Cromwell, and the monarchy restored in 1660.
caption: Causes, practices and effects of war within one kingdom.

alt: Roberts (1955) argued that tactical change between 1560 and 1660 caused larger armies, longer wars and stronger states; Parker (1988) centred fortification and sieges and extended the argument to European expansion; critics ask whether change was gradual and whether states built armies rather than the reverse, shown as a dashed reverse arrow.
caption: The debate links how wars were fought to what they did to governments.

after: ## Worked example: a comparative essay plan
alt: A grid compares the causes of the Thirty Years' War and the Imjin War on long-term instability, rulers' ambitions, ideology, and trigger and escalation. The judgement: many causes combined in the Thirty Years' War; one decision-maker drove the Imjin War; both widened through intervention.
caption: Many combining causes against one ruler's decision.
